AtlasFetch now geocodes addresses, lets you move a zone without losing it, and can draw the street it names. Two new tools, and one new input.

## Added

- **`geocode_address`** — one address to a point, in **South Africa** today. Send `q` on one line, or `address` already split into parts.
  ```
  address · confidence 0.96 · 25 Adderley Street, Cape Town, ZA-WC — dispatch
  street · confidence 0.47 · ambiguous · Long Street, Cape Town, ZA-WC — ask the customer before dispatching
  ```
  The result line applies AtlasFetch's own advice for deliveries. **Dispatch** only on a house-level answer (`address` or `interpolated`) that is not ambiguous, at confidence 0.5 or more. On a `street`-level answer, **ask the recipient for a pin**. When the answer is ambiguous or only suburb-level, **ask the customer**. The description tells the assistant never to present a street-level point as a door. In South Africa most answers *are* street-level, because OpenStreetMap has house numbers on about 13% of street names.

  1 lookup per address, found or not. It takes one address per call on purpose: a delivery list runs row by row, where the user can see what it spends. For thousands of rows, call the API's `POST /geocode/batch` directly.
- **`update_boundary`** — move or reshape one boundary. Its id, name, properties and set stay, so every lookup that matches it keeps returning the same properties. Name it by set and name; if two share a name, the answer lists their ids and asks which. Without this tool, an assistant's only fix for a wrong zone was to delete it and add it again, which loses the id and the properties.
- **`streetGeometry`** on `lookup_location` — each street answer gains the named street's line, trimmed to about 250 m either side of the point. Asking for it adds the street layer automatically. It is off by default, for the same reason as `get_route`'s line: it is hundreds of characters an assistant cannot read.

## Changed

- **A rejected key gets the right advice.** Keys can now be shown again in the AtlasFetch dashboard, and keys made before 12 October 2026 were revoked. The 401 message used to say keys are "shown once" and implied starting over; it now says to copy a live key from the dashboard.
- **"A route costs 10 lookups" now says "on the standard plans".** Some accounts are on custom plans, and `X-Lookups-Remaining` is always the truth for the caller.
- `lookup_location` now points address-to-coordinate questions at `geocode_address`, instead of saying it can't be done.

## Install

**Claude Desktop** — download `atlasfetch-0.3.0.mcpb` below and open it. The API key field is optional.

**Claude Code**

```
claude mcp add atlasfetch -- npx -y atlasfetch-mcp
```

**Other clients** — `npx -y atlasfetch-mcp`, with `ATLASFETCH_API_KEY` in the server's env. See the [README](https://github.com/atlasfetch-dev/atlasfetch-mcp#install).

No signup needed to try it: without a key it uses a shared demo key capped at 1,000 lookups a month across everyone using it. Get your own limits with a free sign-up at [atlasfetch.xyz](https://atlasfetch.xyz/dashboard).
